name: straight_pipe_area_per_length
why: The criterion of the entry to the letter: «sweep -- known circular profile along a straight path of known length, volume computable by hand (area x length)». Here the calculation is pi*10^2*100 = 31415.93, and it comes out to the seventh digit: a straight sweep is not an approximation of anything.
_why_the_path_is_a_list_of_points: `InsertProtrusionSwept4` has `CircularProfile` and `CircularProfileDiameter`: with those the profile sketch is not needed. The path, instead, wants a sketch -- and the operation draws it, from a list of points. It could not be otherwise: in the state of the document sketches have no identifier, so «the third sketch» is something the model has no way to say.

expect.tolerance_why: it is pi*10^2*100: the calculation has pi inside and the tolerance covers the rounding to three decimals

expect.why: THE TRUE VOLUME AND THE THEORETICAL ONE ARE THE SAME NUMBER. Not «close»: equal to the seventh digit. A straight pipe is an exact cylinder, and this case exists so that this can be said -- and to serve as the benchmark for the loft, which is not exact.

expect.tolerance_why: the relative deviation: below the ten-thousandth it is zero
the same number read from the state instead of from the answer
the diameter of the cylindrical face is read from CylinderParams
expect.why: and the face of the pipe really has the requested diameter: the volume alone would also come out right with a wrong diameter and a wrong length that compensate each other

AT THE ELBOW THE CALCULATION DOES NOT ADD UP, AND IT SAYS SO. At the elbow the material overlaps: the true volume is less than area times length. An operation that gave the theoretical one and nothing else would be lying by a few hundred cubic millimetres.
the second pipe is detached from the first: two bodies
